# Bootstrapping of Embeded Standard Setting

## Overview

How to use bootstrapping for ESS


## Fit Embeded Standard Setting

```{r eval = T}
library(EmStanS)
```

```{r eval = T}
fake_data <- genFakeDataSet(ngca = 3, 
               cor_val = 0.2,
               n = 30,
               nlevel = 3,
               ntable = 5,
               npanelist = 5,
               sdinp = 1,
               ecinp = 0,
               100,300)



fake_data

# Or you can use your own data structured by the following table.
```

```{r eval = T}
res <- emstans(data = fake_data,
               grades = c(1, 2),
               location = "Loc_RP50",
               method = "weight",
               smooth = FALSE)

```


## Bootstrapping

`bootstrapping()` resamples one unit's items with replacement (each keeping
its location and modal aligned level) and re-estimates the cut scores in
every sample. One unit at a time; `seed` makes the draws reproducible.

```{r eval = T}
boot_res <- bootstrapping(res, "M1-All", n = 100, seed = 1)
boot_res
```

By default each sample uses the sampled items' locations as candidate cuts
and takes the exact ESS minimum, the same estimator as `emstans()`. The
earlier EmStanS bootstrap, a jittered grid of candidate cuts with a
GAM-smoothed minimum, is available with `grid = "jittered"`:

```{r eval = T}
bootstrapping(res, "M1-All", n = 30, seed = 1, grid = "jittered")
```



## Report

```{r eval = T}
report(boot_res)
```

```{r eval = T}
extract(boot_res)
```
